newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks close down on U.S. raids on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks close down on U.S. raids on Iraq.

text.p: Pakistani stocks, which opened on a positive note, closed down on news of U.S. missile strikes on Iraq, brokers said. They said the index was likely to open lower on Wednesday in thin trading.
The Karachi 100-share index closed 6.80 points, or 0.48 percent, down at 1,413.07 amid 191 losers and 80 gainers. Volume shrank to nine million shares from Monday's 12 million.
"The news of U.S. cruise missile attack against defence targets in Iraq cancelled the positive sentiment prevailing in early morning trade," dealer Ali Raza of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities said.
"The limited movement in the index for the last four sessions indicates some consolidation at these levels," he said.
General Tyre dropped 1.15 rupees to 17.85, Lever Brothers 5.00 to 660, Philips electric 1.00 to 89 and Engro Chemical 3.00 to 141. Pakistan Oxygen rose 7.00 to 120 and PSO 1.00 to 337.
